question: How many Cybertrucks did Tesla deliver in the second quarter of 2026?
grading: Must state that Tesla does not disclose Cybertruck deliveries separately: it reports only 'Model 3/Y' (467,762 delivered in Q2 2026) and 'Other Models' (12,364) combined, and the 10-Q has no Cybertruck unit count. May give the 'Other Models' figure with that label. Fail if a Cybertruck unit number is presented as reported.
answer: Tesla does not disclose Cybertruck deliveries. Its Q2 2026 delivery release reports only Model 3/Y deliveries of 467,762 and 'Other Models' deliveries of 12,364 (total 480,126), and the Q2 2026 update deck and 10-Q give no model-level Cybertruck unit count (Cybertruck appears only in the installed-capacity table, >125,000 per year at Gigafactory Texas, which is not a delivery figure). Any Cybertruck figure would be a third-party estimate. [T18-E1, T18-E2, T18-E3]

output.answer:
**Tesla does not disclose Cybertruck deliveries separately, so there's no official Cybertruck-only figure for Q2 2026.**

What Tesla reported (Q2 2026 production & deliveries, released July 2, 2026):

| Category | Production | Deliveries |
|---|---|---|
| Model 3 / Model Y | 442,936 | 467,762 |
| Other Models (Cybertruck, Semi, remaining Model S/X) | 8,822 | 12,364 |
| **Total** | **451,758** | **480,126** |

So the Cybertruck is buried inside the **12,364 "Other Models" deliveries** alongside the Tesla Semi and whatever Model S/X inventory remained (both S and X were discontinued earlier in 2026). Any specific Cybertruck number for the quarter would be a third-party estimate, not a Tesla disclosure — third-party tracking put Cybertruck at roughly ~20,000 units for all of 2025, and commentary around the Q2 print described the truck as "not selling well."

Sources:
- https://ir.tesla.com/press-release/tesla-second-quarter-2026-production-deliveries-and-deployments
- https://electrek.co/2026/07/02/tesla-q2-2026-deliveries-480126
- https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/02/tesla-tsla-q2-2026-vehicle-delivery-production.html

Note: I can't verify these figures independently beyond the reports returned — Tesla's own IR release is the authoritative source, and it only gives the combined "Other Models" number.
